API

The api app: the REST API for articles, with token authentication.

api.serializers

The REST API’s serializer, which turns articles into JSON and checks the JSON that callers send.

class api.serializers.ArticleSerializer(*args, **kwargs)[source]

Turns an article into JSON, and checks the JSON sent to create or update one.

A caller sends the title, the content, and, for a new article, its publication’s ID, or null for an independent article. The author, approval, and creation time are set by the application.

To check the publication of a new article, the serializer needs the request in its context, since the caller is the author.

Variables:

author – The author’s username, which is easier to read than their ID.

validate_publication(publication)[source]

Refuses a publication the article may not have.

A new article can be independent, or for a publication its author works for. An existing article keeps its publication, so sending a different one is refused.

Parameters:

publication – The Publication sent, or None for an independent article.

Returns:

The publication, if the article may have it.

Raises:

ValidationError – If an existing article’s publication would change, or a new article’s publication is not one its author works for.

api.views

The REST API’s article endpoints.

Every endpoint in this file needs a valid token in the Authorization header, the default for Django REST Framework (DRF) views set in REST_FRAMEWORK in settings.py. A request with a missing or invalid token gets 401 Unauthorized before the view runs.

The endpoint that gives users their tokens is not defined here. It is DRF’s ready-made token view, routed in urls.py, which returns a user’s token for their username and password.

api.views.fields_not_valid(errors)[source]

The response to data with missing or invalid fields, listing each field and what is wrong with it.

Parameters:

errors – The errors for each field, such as a serializer’s errors.

Returns:

A 400 Bad Request response, with the errors.

api.views.contains(articles, article)[source]

Whether a queryset of articles, such as the ones a user can change, includes this article.

Parameters:

  • articles – A queryset of Article objects.

  • article – The Article object to look for.

Returns:

True if the queryset includes the article, otherwise False.

api.views.articles(request, *args, **kwargs)[source]

GET lists every approved article, newest first.

POST creates an article written by the caller, which starts as pending. Only journalists can create articles.

Parameters:

request – The API request. For POST, the new article as JSON.

Returns:

For GET, the approved articles. For POST, 201 Created, with the new article; 403 Forbidden if the caller is not a journalist; or 400 Bad Request, with each missing or invalid field.

api.views.subscribed(request, *args, **kwargs)[source]

GET lists the approved articles from the caller’s subscriptions, the same articles as on a reader’s dashboard. Only readers have subscriptions.

Parameters:

request – The API request.

Returns:

The articles from the caller’s subscriptions, or 403 Forbidden if the caller is not a reader.

api.views.pending(request, *args, **kwargs)[source]

GET lists the pending articles the caller can approve, oldest first, so the ones that have waited longest come first: a publication’s articles for its editors, and a journalist’s own independent articles for them. Only editors and journalists can approve articles.

Parameters:

request – The API request.

Returns:

The pending articles the caller can approve, or 403 Forbidden if the caller cannot approve articles.

api.views.article_detail(request, *args, **kwargs)[source]

GET returns one article.

PUT updates an article, sending every field, and PATCH updates only the fields sent. Either can approve a pending article by sending "approved": true.

DELETE deletes an article.

Each method follows the same rules as the website.

Parameters:

  • request – The API request. For PUT and PATCH, the article’s fields as JSON.

  • article_id – The article’s ID, from the URL.

Returns:

For GET, PUT, and PATCH, the article. For DELETE, 204 No Content. A change the caller may not make gets 403 Forbidden, and data that is not valid gets 400 Bad Request, each with a message saying why.

Raises:

Http404 – If the article does not exist, or the caller may not read it.
